strengths: Addresses an important efficiency bottleneck in multimodal models. Reducing visual prefixes from 576 to approximately 40 tokens while retaining the language backbone offers substantial potential computational savings.
Evaluation covers six benchmarks and both 7B and 13B LLaVA-1.5 models. The fine-tuned compressed models preserve strong performance on ScienceQA and POPE despite aggressive compression.

The ablations provide useful evidence for the components. In Table 3, training-free PruMerge achieves 54.00 TextVQA versus 47.96 for the best spatial sampler. Table 4 shows that token supplementation improves MME from 1221.6 to 1350.3 over selection alone.
The overall pipeline is understandable and illustrated clearly. The manuscript attributes its underlying models, training data, benchmarks, and prior pruning and merging methods.
weaknesses: The accuracy-preservation claims are overstated. Table 1 reports VQAv2 declining from 78.5 to 72.0 for 7B, MMBench from 67.7 to 62.3 for 13B, and MME from 1510.7 to 1350.3 for 7B. Training-free POPE also falls from 85.9 to 76.2 in Table 5. These losses may be worthwhile for substantial compression, but they are consequential rather than merely marginal. Accuracy-versus-token-budget curves are needed to characterize the tradeoff beyond one aggressive operating point.

The comparisons do not sufficiently establish the contribution beyond existing attention-based pruning and key-based merging. Table 3 primarily compares against retaining the first tokens or spatial subsampling; it lacks fixed-budget top-k class-attention selection and an adapted ToMe-style baseline. Consequently, the benefit of IQR-based adaptivity remains unclear. Although Table 3 fairly compares training-free variants, equivalent comparisons after fine-tuning are missing, while the main results use an additional LoRA epoch.

The practical efficiency evidence is incomplete. Table 2 explicitly provides roofline estimates for LLM prefill rather than measured execution. There are no end-to-end latency, throughput, or peak-memory measurements accounting for the vision encoder, selection and clustering overhead, decoding, and variable-length batching. The estimates support potential savings but do not establish the realized deployment benefit central to the paper.

Important implementation details are missing or inconsistent. Algorithm 1 excludes the selected center from its neighbor candidates and replaces it with an unnormalized weighted sum, whereas the prose describes supplementing retained tokens through weighted averaging. This affects both feature scale and information retention. The neighborhood size k, attention-head aggregation, handling of overlapping neighborhoods, and LoRA training configuration are also unspecified. With code and checkpoints only promised, these ambiguities materially hinder reproduction.
